side_a: CC 5.3.3.1 On epoch roll the DEK changes, so a reset counter lives in a different keyspace
side_b: CC 5.3.3.1 Substrate MUST reject a chunk-append whose `(stream_id, seq)` collides with an existing sealed chunk (the replay and forking guard).
note: CC 5.3.3.2.5 sets the nonce counter equal to the header chunk_seq. Read with the first side, chunk_seq restarts at each epoch (and only a restart makes the forced roll before 2^32 avoid a wrap); read with the second side and CC 5.3.3.3 (leaves in seq order, tree_size the chunk count of the whole stream) seq is unique across the stream and never restarts. The two builds derive different nonces from epoch two on, or one refuses the other's chunk 0 as a collision. Nothing states whether chunk_seq is per epoch or per stream; CC 3.3.13 (sequence_start, HLS sequence numbers) leans per stream
